chiefComplaint: Persistent fever and fatigue for six days
historyOfPresentIllness: Fever began six days ago, initially low grade and now reaching 38.9 C in the evenings. Associated with marked fatigue, generalised body ache and reduced appetite. No cough, no urinary symptoms, no loose stools. Took paracetamol with temporary relief. Symptoms have not improved despite a course of over-the-counter medication started on day three.

symptoms.name: Fever
symptoms.notes: Peaks in the evening, settles partially with paracetamol

symptoms.name: Fatigue
symptoms.notes: Unable to complete a full day of work

symptomTimeline.description: Low-grade fever begins in the evening.

symptomTimeline.label: Day 2
symptomTimeline.description: Fatigue develops; patient stops attending work.

symptomTimeline.label: Day 3
symptomTimeline.description: Started over-the-counter paracetamol and a multivitamin.

symptomTimeline.description: Body ache and reduced appetite reported.

symptomTimeline.label: Day 6
symptomTimeline.description: Fever persists at 38.9 C; consultation requested.

chiefComplaint: Review of renal function panel and 24-hour Holter
historyOfPresentIllness: Attends to review investigations arranged at the last visit. Reports occasional palpitations lasting a few minutes, mostly at rest, with no chest pain or syncope. Breathlessness on climbing one flight of stairs is unchanged. Urine output subjectively normal. No swelling of the legs.

chiefComplaint: Glycaemic control review, ankle swelling since last visit
historyOfPresentIllness: Attends for a diabetes follow-up. Reports that ankle swelling has partially improved since furosemide was started four weeks ago but returns by the end of the day. Fasting glucose readings at home range between 160 and 210 mg/dL. Reports increased thirst and nocturia twice per night. No chest pain or breathlessness.

symptoms.notes: Worse by evening, partially relieved by elevation

chiefComplaint: Fitness assessment prior to elective cholecystectomy
historyOfPresentIllness: Referred by the surgical team for pre-operative assessment before an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy scheduled in three weeks. Reports two episodes of right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals in the past two months. No jaundice, no fever. Cardiac symptoms are stable; walks two kilometres daily without chest pain.

symptoms.name: Right upper quadrant pain
symptoms.notes: Triggered by fatty meals, lasts about an hour

symptomTimeline.description: Ultrasound confirms gallstones; surgical referral made.

historyOfPresentIllness: Reports that headache episodes have increased from two per month to six per month over the past three months. Episodes are unilateral, throbbing, lasting six to twelve hours, with nausea and light sensitivity. No aura. Triggers appear to include missed meals and disturbed sleep. Over-the-counter analgesia is now less effective.

historyOfPresentIllness: Attends with a three-month menstrual diary. Cycles remain irregular at 38 to 55 days. Reports weight gain of three kilograms over six months and increasing facial hair. No galactorrhoea. Currently trying to conceive for eight months.
